The estate can recover damages for the injuries caused by the driver's negligence, but the pedestrian's refusal of a life-saving transfusion may be treated as a superseding cause or as contributory/comparative negligence, limiting recovery for the death. Many jurisdictions would allow recovery for the initial injury and possibly the "loss of chance," but not full wrongful-death damages, because the victim's unreasonable refusal broke the causal chain to death. The exact outcome depends on jurisdiction, but the driver is unlikely to be liable for the full death damages.
